name: Government of Kuwait

summary.text: After Iraq's August 1990 invasion, the government of Kuwait funded Citizens for a Free Kuwait, a group whose main contractor was the public-relations firm Hill & Knowlton. Accounts by Stauber and Rampton say the Kuwaiti government channelled $11.9 million to the group over six months, that its only other funding was $17,861 from 78 individuals, and that $10.8 million went to Hill & Knowlton in fees. The firm's campaign included the October 1990 testimony of 'Nayirah', later identified as the daughter of Kuwait's ambassador to the United States, to a congressional caucus. Hill & Knowlton denied wrongdoing.

facts.claim: Stauber and Rampton wrote that over six months the Kuwaiti government channelled $11.9 million to Citizens for a Free Kuwait, whose only other funding totalled $17,861 from 78 individuals, and that virtually all of the group's budget, $10.8 million, went to Hill & Knowlton in fees.
facts.quote: Over the next six months, the Kuwaiti government channeled $11.9 million dollars to Citizens for a Free Kuwait, whose only other funding totalled $17,861 from 78 individuals.

facts.claim: Other accounts give different figures for the campaign's cost: $11.5 million paid to Hill & Knowlton, an estimated $12 million, or close to $12 million from the Emir.
facts.quote: the group paid Hill and Knowlton $11.5 million

facts.claim: Hill & Knowlton helped prepare the October 1990 testimony of a fifteen-year-old identified only as 'Nayirah' who said she had seen Iraqi soldiers remove babies from incubators; in 1992 it emerged that she was the daughter of Saud Al-Sabah, Kuwait's ambassador to the United States.
facts.quote: she was the daughter of Saud Al-Sabah, the Kuwaiti ambassador to the United States

facts.claim: Hill & Knowlton denied any wrongdoing in the Kuwait campaign and sued in a German court seeking a retraction from the public-affairs programme 'Monitor', which had reported the story.

facts.claim: O'Dwyer's reported in June 2025 that Hill & Knowlton terminated its Foreign Agents Registration Act registration with the Justice Department, listing Citizens for a Free Kuwait among its past clients.

openQuestions: Site claim tested: 'Kuwait's government began channelling $11.9 million to a front group whose only other money was $17,861' — supported by Stauber and Rampton's account only; the underlying FARA filings were not located. Figures in other outlets range from $10 million to $12 million.
Site claim tested: that Nayirah 'had been coached' — the sources say Hill & Knowlton helped write her statement and practise its delivery; the word 'coached' is the site's.
No Justice Department FARA record for Hill & Knowlton's Kuwait account was opened; the owner may wish to check the FARA eFile database.
